contexts.correctionCheck: Publisher and PubMed records and exact-title notice searches checked. No identified notice resolves the specified method, control or label issues; this is not exhaustive correction or replication surveillance.
contexts.finding: Peripheral challenges evoked neural readouts, while selected neural manipulations changed circulating cytokines. Activation improved high-dose endotoxin survival but increased bacterial tissue load in a different live-infection protocol. A complete descending immune circuit is not identified.
limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

FOS labeling is an activity-associated marker; Vglut2-cre bulk GCaMP6s is a population calcium signal, not a DBH-specific spike recording. Photometry uses saline on day 4 and LPS on day 5 in the same animals. Vagotomized mice form a separate group after two weeks of recovery; a matched abdominal sham is not explicitly specified in the reviewed procedure. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Fos-based TRAP2 labeling is followed by at least four weeks before functional rechallenge to restore LPS sensitivity. LPS-TRAPed, Dbh-cre, Vglut2-cre and Vgat-cre populations are not identical. Dbh expression does not measure norepinephrine release or identify a unique molecular mediator.

For standard cytokine chemogenetics, Methods specify CNO at 2 mg/kg twelve hours and 1 mg/kg one hour before challenge; schematics and captions show only the one-hour pretreatment. mCherry controls receive CNO. Saline/LPS tests use the same cohort at least seven days apart, whereas hM3Dq/hM4Di versus mCherry comparisons use separate groups. Blood ELISA at two hours does not identify cytokine-producing cells.

Cre-defined nodose activation perturbs marker-defined neurons; it is not selective activation of the TRPA1 channel or CALCA peptide. TRPA1 neurons include different stimulus-responsive subgroups. Extended Data 8e shows two IL-10/fat co-responders among 63 neurons, which the authors did not consider further. Universal zero overlap is unsupported.

Injected cytokines and extraintestinal perfusion have different doses, routes and recording windows. The response classifier uses baseline median absolute deviation, a mean modified z-score above 1.6 and peak fluorescence of at least 1%. Selected, normalized responder heatmaps are not an unbiased full-population distribution. Table 1 gives dentate BrdUrd estimates of 4308, 3288, 1968, 2748, 1896, 1176, 780, 876, 420, 336 and 228 for animals 1-11. Mixed species, dose accumulation, age and survival prevent a pooled age-specific production rate. The single-dose two-hour age contrast has only one young and one middle-aged animal against three aged animals.

The neuronal-marker means concern the four five-injection animals 1, 3, 5 and 6: TOAD-64 1230.5 +/- 436.9, NSE 822.1 +/- 345.9 and calbindin 793.2 +/- 232.9. Printed-PDF agreement with the HTML table has not been verified.

BrdUrd profiles in a region corresponding to the rodent rostral migratory stream, occasional mitotic figures and TOAD-64 profiles motivate an olfactory-neuron interpretation. They do not track movement to the olfactory bulb, common ancestry, arrival, synaptic integration or sensory function.

The abstract reports fewer new astroglial cells; the described neuronal examples lack GFAP. A complete GFAP count and animal-level fraction are not provided. Antibody-omission and confocal checks address staining artifacts, not a demonstrated founder lineage.

source.title: Nature and fate of proliferative cells in the hippocampal dentate gyrus during the life span of the rhesus monkey

limitations: Twelve rhesus monkeys were labeled at reported ages of six months to eleven years; Table 1 gives ages at death of seven months to seventeen years. This is a mixed developmental and adult sample, not twelve animals labeled after puberty. Age at death cannot substitute for age at injection.

Between 500 and 1000 sections per animal were screened across major brain regions and spinal cord, followed by brightfield or Nomarski examination with a 63x oil objective. The estimated million cells per specimen is not an exact neuronal denominator, random whole-brain census or statistical upper bound on rare births. Table 1 specifies 8-micrometre sections and every second to tenth section depending on region size.

Heavy labeling was calibrated separately in each case from glial, endothelial or peripheral cells, usually more than 15-30 silver grains per nucleus. Light-microscopic autoradiography exposure was 12-18 weeks and electron-microscopic exposure exceeded 24 weeks. A common fixed threshold cannot be imposed retrospectively. Occasional neuronal profiles with fewer than five or six grains were not classified as newborn; artifact or DNA repair was proposed without a repair assay.

Methods specifies six early developmental animals with one intravenous 5-10 mCi/kg tritiated-thymidine injection and one-hour survival. Table 1 instead prints one day for these rows. The eleven additional animals are described as surviving five weeks to two years, while Table 1 includes fourteen days, three years and six years. No adult one-hour cohort is documented; early developmental sampling cannot supply an adult short-interval null.

Figure 12B is described as an oligodendroglial type in Results but as resting microglia in the caption. Its specific subtype remains unresolved. No labeled profile had reported neuronal ultrastructure or synapses in the examined sections; this sampling-limited null does not prove absence of all neuronal precursor potential.

The discussion calls sixteen injections to four adult animals equivalent to independent labeling experiments. Repeated exposures share animals and cumulative label windows. The eleven-of-twelve-month coverage is also pooled across animals and ages, not a matched adult seasonal experiment. No formal rare-neuron detection bound or exact cessation age is calculated.

Gliogenesis, replacement and stable-neuron memory roles are interpretations. No paired birth/death census identifies population feedback, and no functional or behavioral test establishes that neuron turnover impairs memory. The adult autoradiographic null remains distinct from a universal prohibition on adult neurogenesis.

limitations: Eleven animals comprise nine Macaca fascicularis and two M. mulatta, aged 5-23 years. Table 1 provides sex, age, injection number and survival per animal, but site, assay-specific sampling and raw counts are unavailable. All three 23-year-old animals are male M. fascicularis.

BrdUrd was 75 mg/kg intraperitoneally, one to five injections separated by 24 hours. Five single-injection animals survived two hours; six animals with three or five injections survived one or two weeks after the last injection. One Results paragraph instead says after the first injection. This timing conflict remains unresolved.

Methods explicitly states that two hours permits S-phase labeling but not completed mitosis or migration. All three 23-year-old animals have only this two-hour interval. The reported oldest-age BrdU and TOAD-64 profiles do not establish birthdated neuronal differentiation at that age.

The modified optical fractionator uses coded slides and every twelfth 40-micrometre section, excluding the outermost focal plane. Estimates are not raw cell counts or instantaneous birth rates. Processed thickness, sampling implementation, raw stacks and animal-by-marker data are required for reproduction.

Table 1 gives dentate BrdUrd estimates of 4308, 3288, 1968, 2748, 1896, 1176, 780, 876, 420, 336 and 228 for animals 1-11. Mixed species, dose accumulation, age and survival prevent a pooled age-specific production rate. The single-dose two-hour age contrast has only one young and one middle-aged animal against three aged animals.

The neuronal-marker means concern the four five-injection animals 1, 3, 5 and 6: TOAD-64 1230.5 +/- 436.9, NSE 822.1 +/- 345.9 and calbindin 793.2 +/- 232.9. These are separate overlapping marker assays, not disjoint cell populations or universal fractions. NeuN is illustrated in animal 1; a complete quantified NeuN census is not supplied.

The PMC HTML Table 2 lists M. fascicularis group sizes of 4 young, 4 middle-aged and 2 aged, plus 2 middle-aged M. mulatta. These total 12 rather than the 11 Table 1 animals; Table 1 instead has 2 young and 3 aged animals. The reported F(2,5)=154.2 cannot be reproduced from an identified animal-level analysis. Printed-PDF agreement with the HTML table has not been verified.

TOAD-64 profiles indicate an immature neuronal phenotype under the marker assumptions. Figure 1F uses TOAD-64 and a DNA counterstain, not BrdUrd birth labeling. Its cells cannot be treated as an independently birthdated lineage or as an image from an aged animal; the caption identifies animal 1.

BrdUrd profiles in a region corresponding to the rodent rostral migratory stream, occasional mitotic figures and TOAD-64 profiles motivate an olfactory-neuron interpretation. They do not track movement to the olfactory bulb, common ancestry, arrival, synaptic integration or sensory function.

The abstract reports fewer new astroglial cells; the described neuronal examples lack GFAP. A complete GFAP count and animal-level fraction are not provided. Antibody-omission and confocal checks address staining artifacts, not a demonstrated founder lineage.

Cortisol, learning, stress, enrichment and functional circuit activity were not measured or manipulated. The discussion draws on other species and publications to propose survival, glucocorticoid and memory mechanisms. It does not supply matched primate causal evidence or a universal prerequisite.

This study and Kornack and Rakic (1999) use different doses, routes, survival schedules, marker assays and counting procedures. Agreement on some neuronal colabels does not make their numerical rates or age groups interchangeable. The reviewed 1985/1988 autoradiographic protocols differ in sampling and phenotype criteria; matched detection sensitivity remains unresolved.

All main scientific text, Materials and Methods, Tables 1-2 and the Figure 1 caption were read in PMC HTML; all six panels of the archived figure were visually inspected. The publisher PDF, raw measurements and assay-level manifest were not obtained. Table 2 reporting concerns are verified against HTML only.

rationale.statement: Young and middle-aged animals examined after longer intervals had dentate BrdUrd colabels with neuronal markers. The four five-injection animals provide TOAD-64, NSE and calbindin estimates, while NeuN is illustrated separately. These findings do not establish differentiated newborn neurons in the two-hour aged cohort.
